content: Meningococcal disease is an illness caused by the bacterium Neisseria meningitidis. Individuals with meningococcal disease can transmit the bacteria to others through close personal contact, such as living in the same household or kissing. Immediate medical attention is required for anyone diagnosed with meningococcal disease. The symptoms of this disease vary depending on the specific type of illness. For meningitis, symptoms include a sudden onset of fever, headache, and a stiff neck. Additional symptoms may include nausea, vomiting, increased sensitivity to light, and confusion. In children and infants, the signs may differ and include inactivity, irritability, vomiting, or poor reflexes. When meningococcal disease leads to septicemia, symptoms include fatigue, vomiting, chills, severe aches and pains, rapid breathing, diarrhea, and the appearance of a dark rash. Anyone can contract meningococcal disease, but certain populations are at higher risk. People living in or traveling to specific regions, such as the meningitis belt of sub-Saharan Africa, are more likely to be affected. This region experiences the highest rates of meningococcal disease globally, particularly during the dry season from December to June. Travelers who spend significant time with local populations in this area, especially during outbreaks, are at increased risk. Additionally, participants in the Hajj or Umrah pilgrimages in Saudi Arabia are more susceptible to the disease. The most effective way to prevent meningococcal disease is through vaccination. The MenACWY vaccine is routinely administered to pre-teens and teenagers in the United States. All children aged 11 to 12 should receive a dose of the MenACWY vaccine, followed by a booster shot at age 16. Adolescents and young adults may also receive the MenB vaccine, ideally between the ages of 16 and 18. Younger children and adults may require the MenACWY vaccine depending on their travel plans. Some individuals who have been vaccinated previously may need a booster shot. It takes approximately 7 to 10 days after vaccination for maximum protection against the disease to develop. Travelers should consult their healthcare provider well in advance of their trip to ensure they are adequately protected. It is important to determine whether a MenACWY vaccine is recommended for the intended travel destination. Currently, there are no specific recommendations for receiving the MenB vaccine before traveling. However, individuals traveling to Saudi Arabia for the Hajj or Umrah pilgrimages must provide proof of MenACWY vaccination. This vaccine may also be referred to as the tetravalent or quadrivalent meningococcal vaccine.
